43056-history-of-the-jews-vol-1-of-6.creator: Heinrich Graetz
43056-history-of-the-jews-vol-1-of-6.description: A book by Heinrich Graetz. bserve a phenomenon, which has developed and asserted itself in spite of all laws of nature, and we behold a culture which, notwithstanding unspeakable hostility against its exponents, has nevertheless profoundly modified the organism of nations.

arxiv-1810-02099.title: Longest Property-Preserved Common Factor
arxiv-1810-02099.creator: Lorraine A.K Ayad, Giulia Bernardini, Roberto Grossi, Costas S. Iliopoulos, Nadia Pisanti, Solon P. Pissis, Giovanna Rosone
arxiv-1810-02099.description: Abstract In this paper we introduce a new family of string processing problems. We are given two or more strings and we are asked to compute a factor common to all strings that preserves a specific property and has maximal length.

arxiv-1905-08083.title: Geometries in perturbative quantum field theory
arxiv-1905-08083.creator: Oliver Schnetz
arxiv-1905-08083.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Oliver Schnetz. In perturbative quantum field theory one encounters certain, very specific geometries over the integers. These perturbative quantum geometries determine the number contents of the amplitude considered. In the article ‘Modular forms in quantum field theory’ F. Brown and the author report on a first list of perturbative quantum geometries using the c 2 c_{2} -invariant in φ 4 \varphi^{4} theory. A main tool was denominator reduction which allowed the authors to examine graphs up to loop order (first Betti number) 10.

arxiv-2002-04563.title: Mathematical Foundations of Regression Methods for Approximating the Forward Initial Margin
arxiv-2002-04563.creator: Lucia Cipolina-Kun, Simone Caenazzo, Ksenia Ponomareva
arxiv-2002-04563.description: Abstract † † corresponding author: lucia.kun@bristol.ac.uk The modelling of forward initial margin poses a challenging problem as it requires the implementation of a nested Monte Carlo simulation, which is computationally intractable. Abundant literature has been published on approximation methods aiming to reduce the dimensionality of the problem, the most popular ones being the family of regression methods.

arxiv-2005-07020.title: On t t -core and self-conjugate ( 2 ​ t − 1 ) (2t-1) -core partitions in arithmetic progressions
arxiv-2005-07020.creator: Kathrin Bringmann, Ben Kane, Joshua Males
arxiv-2005-07020.description: Abstract . We extend recent results of Ono and Raji, relating the number of self-conjugate 7 7 -core partitions to Hurwitz class numbers. Furthermore, we give a combinatorial explanation for the curious equality 2 ​ sc 7 ⁡ ( 8 ​ n + 1 ) = c 4 ⁡ ( 7 ​ n + 2 ) 2\operatorname{sc}_{7}(8n+1)=\operatorname{c}_{4}(7n+2) .

arxiv-2204-09616.title: Assembly Planning from Observations under Physical Constraints
arxiv-2204-09616.creator: Thomas Chabal, Robin Strudel, Etienne Arlaud, Jean Ponce, Cordelia Schmid
arxiv-2204-09616.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Thomas Chabal, Robin Strudel, Etienne Arlaud, Jean Ponce, Cordelia Schmid. This paper addresses the problem of copying an unknown assembly of primitives with known shape and appearance using information extracted from a single photograph by an off-the-shelf procedure for object detection and pose estimation. The proposed algorithm uses a simple combination of physical stability constraints, convex optimization and Monte Carlo tree search to plan assemblies as sequences of pick-and-place operations represented by STRIPS operators.

arxiv-2205-03732.title: Developing a semiclassical Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin theory for α − 𝒯 3 \alpha-\mathcal{T}_{3} model
arxiv-2205-03732.creator: Kathy Blaise 1 , Chinedu Ejiogu 1 , Andrii Iurov 1 , Liubov Zhemchuzhna 1,2 , Godfrey Gumbs 2,3 , and Danhong Huang 4,5
arxiv-2205-03732.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kathy Blaise 1 , Chinedu Ejiogu 1 , Andrii Iurov 1 , Liubov Zhemchuzhna 1,2 , Godfrey Gumbs 2,3 , and Danhong Huang 4,5. We have developed a complete semiclassical Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) theory for α − 𝒯 3 \alpha-\mathcal{T}_{3} model which describes a wide class of existing pseudospin-1 Dirac cone materials.

arxiv-2302-12215.title: A coloring of the plane without monochromatic right triangles
arxiv-2302-12215.creator: Balázs Bursics, Péter Komjáth
arxiv-2302-12215.description: Abstract We give a full, correct proof of the following result, earlier claimed in [ 1 ] . If the Continuum Hypothesis holds then there is a coloring of the plane with countably many colors, with no monocolored right triangle. One 1 1 1 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification. Primary 03E50 Secondary 51M04, 05D10.

arxiv-2406-11240.title: The Benefits of Power Regularization in Cooperative Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2406-11240.creator: Michelle Li, Michael Dennis
arxiv-2406-11240.description: Abstract . Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithms, trained only to optimize task reward, can lead to a concentration of power where the failure or adversarial intent of a single agent could decimate the reward of every agent in the system.

arxiv-2408-17323.title: Dark and bright sides of the Broad Line Region clouds as seen in the FeII emission of SDSS RM 102
arxiv-2408-17323.creator: Alberto Floris, Ashwani Pandey, Bozena Czerny, Mary Loli Martinez Aldama, Swayamtrupta Panda, Paola Marziani, Raj Prince
arxiv-2408-17323.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alberto Floris, Ashwani Pandey, Bozena Czerny, Mary Loli Martinez Aldama, Swayamtrupta Panda, Paola Marziani, Raj Prince. Contamination from singly ionized iron emission is one of the greatest obstacles to determining the intensity of emission lines in the UV and optical wavelength ranges. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the Fe ii emission in the bright quasar RM 102, based on the most recent version of the CLOUDY software, with the goal of simultaneously reproducing UV and optical Fe ii emission.

arxiv-2412-18316.title: Data-Driven Self-Supervised Graph Representation Learning
arxiv-2412-18316.creator: Ahmed E. Samy, Zekarias T. Kefato, Šarūnas Girdzijauskas
arxiv-2412-18316.description: Abstract Self-supervised graph representation learning (SSGRL) is a representation learning paradigm used to reduce or avoid manual labeling. An essential part of SSGRL is graph data augmentation. Existing methods usually rely on heuristics commonly identified through trial and error and are effective only within some application domains. Also, it is not clear why one heuristic is better than another.

arxiv-2502-17405.title: Function-Space Learning Rates
arxiv-2502-17405.creator: Edward Milsom, Ben Anson, Laurence Aitchison
arxiv-2502-17405.description: Abstract We consider layerwise function-space learning rates, which measure the magnitude of the change in a neural network’s output function in response to an update to a parameter tensor. This contrasts with traditional learning rates, which describe the magnitude of changes in parameter space.

arxiv-2503-15464.title: The 200 Gbps Challenge: Imagining HL-LHC analysis facilities
arxiv-2503-15464.creator: \firstname Alexander \lastname Held \fnsep, \firstname Sam \lastname Albin, \firstname Garhan \lastname Attebury, \firstname Kenneth \lastname Bloom, \firstname Brian \lastname Bockelman, \firstname Lincoln \lastname Bryant, \firstname Kyungeon \lastname Choi, \firstname Kyle \lastname Cranmer, \fir
arxiv-2503-15464.description: Abstract The IRIS-HEP software institute, as a contributor to the broader HEP Python ecosystem, is developing scalable analysis infrastructure and software tools to address the upcoming HL-LHC computing challenges with new approaches and paradigms, driven by our vision of what HL-LHC analysis will require.

arxiv-2510-13808.title: VisCoP : Visual Probing for Video Domain Adaptation of Vision Language Models
arxiv-2510-13808.creator: Dominick Reilly Manish Kumar Govind Le Xue Srijan Das
arxiv-2510-13808.description: Abstract Large Vision Language Models (VLMs) excel at general visual reasoning tasks, but their performance degrades sharply when deployed in novel domains with substantial distribution shifts compared to what was seen during pretraining. Existing approaches to adapt VLMs to novel target domains rely on finetuning standard VLM components.

pmc-11346417.title: Microplastics and gut microbiomes impact on Yunnan snub-nosed monkeys in the Three Parallel Rivers region in China
pmc-11346417.creator: Wancai Xia, Jiajie Zhou, Zhongwei Lu, Liang Li, Yuan Zhang, Shiyuan Fan, Ali Krzton, Dayong Li
pmc-11346417.description: BackgroundMicroplastics (MPs) has been rapidly increasing and interacting with wildlife. As the highest altitudes inhabited non-human primate, Yunnan snub-nosed monkey (Rhinopithecus bieti) have been proven to be an umbrella and flagship species to indicate ecosystem changes and help develop environmental management strategies.

pmc-12555881.title: How change in behaviour influences the impact of mpox vaccination among men who have sex with men
pmc-12555881.creator: M Xiridou, D van Wees, P Adam, F Miura, E Op de Coul, M Reitsema, J de Wit, B van Benthem, J Wallinga
pmc-12555881.description: BackgroundThe 2022 outbreak of mpox subclade IIb in the Netherlands affected primarily men who have sex with men (MSM). The recent outbreak of subclade Ib in African countries and its introduction in Europe and America have raised concerns about future mpox outbreaks.

pmc-12566542.title: Association Between Alexithymia, Sexual Dysfunctions, and Dyadic Adjustment in Obsessive–Compulsive Disorder
pmc-12566542.creator: Tunahan Sun, Gonca Karakuş, Lut Tamam, Mehmet Emin Demirkol, Zeynep Namlı, Caner Yeşiloğlu
pmc-12566542.description: Background and Objectives: Chronic mental disorders may negatively affect sexual functioning and dyadic adjustment. This study aimed to investigate the associations between alexithymia, sexual dysfunctions, and dyadic adjustment in patients with obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) and to compare these variables with those of healthy controls.

pmc-12597623.title: CART in MCL: risk and reward?
pmc-12597623.creator: Toby A Eyre
pmc-12597623.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). es (CRRs, 68%) in patients with heavily pretreated MCL who had all received a prior covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor (cBTKi). Following ZUMA2, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approvals for this product were slightly different, with a broader FDA approval including any patients with relapsed or refractory MCL regardless of a patient’s prior exposure to a BTKi whereas the EMA approval requires prior BTKi exposure.

pmc-12949831.title: Comparative Study on the Effect of Vitamin D Deficiency on Platelet Indices in COVID‐19 and Hepatitis C Patients; an Observational Comparative Study
pmc-12949831.creator: Mohammad Motaghi, Kazem Ghaffari, Mahroo Mansori, Ali Ghasemi
pmc-12949831.description: Background and AimsDespite growing interest in the role of vitamin D in various infectious diseases, limited evidence exists regarding its association with platelet (PLT) parameters in patients with COVID‐19 and Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) infection. This study aims to assess the relationship between serum vitamin D levels and PLT indices in patients with COVID‐19 and chronic HCV.

pmc-12979087.title: Fatty liver index in early pregnancy predicts the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus
pmc-12979087.creator: Juping Wei, Ning Ma, Liwei Bai, Qiang Lu
pmc-12979087.description: ObjectiveTo examine the ability of the fatty liver index (FLI) in early pregnancy to predict the risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM).MethodsA total of 1,004 women underwent metabolism characterization at weeks 8–12 of gestation and a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) at weeks 24–28 of gestation.

pmc-13089657.title: Overexpression or Activation of Potassium Channel TASK-3 Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells and Restores Visual Function in Optic Nerve Crush
pmc-13089657.creator: Jiali Zhang, Xinyi Chen, Jing Ji, Pengfan Chen, Jiaxin Yao, Ruotian Jiang, Longqian Liu, Xiangyi Wen
pmc-13089657.description: PurposeThis study explored in a mouse model whether activation or upregulation of the two-pore domain potassium channel tandem pore domain acid-sensitive potassium channel 3 (TASK-3) in retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) could protect RGCs and reverse the vision loss arising through optic nerve injury.MethodsTASK-3 activity was assessed using patch-clamp electrophysiology.

pmc-13159361.title: Fractional shot noise of an SU(N) Kondo system
pmc-13159361.creator: Damian Krychowski, Stanisław Lipiński
pmc-13159361.description: We consider transport through a multilevel interacting quantum dot (N-QD) in the Kondo regime. Using the Kotliar–Ruckentein slave boson approach (SBMFA) for an N-level Anderson model, we define effectively noninteracting quasiparticles of the SU(N) Kondo system (N = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Kondo resonance transmission coefficients determine linear noise describing quasiparticle partitioning.

pmc-13225994.title: Expanded National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale and posterior circulation-specific stroke scales help address assessment blind spots in posterior circulation ischemic stroke
pmc-13225994.creator: Qi Han, Mei-Hua Han
pmc-13225994.description: The National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale is the most widely used bedside scale for assessing neurological deficit severity in acute stroke and guiding early clinical decision-making. However, it has important limitations in posterior circulation stroke, particularly in cases involving the brainstem and cerebellum.

pmc-13334407.title: A Prospective Assessment of Hearing Threshold Variability in Personal Listening Device Users
pmc-13334407.creator: Bhushan Chauhan, Shweta Godara, Aishwarya Jayan, Kirtika Gupta, Ginni Datta
pmc-13334407.description: Background and aimThe increasing use of personal listening devices (PLDs), particularly in-ear earphones, has raised concerns regarding their potential adverse effects on auditory health among young adults. Prolonged exposure to high-intensity recreational sound is considered a major risk factor for noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL).

pmc-13358382.title: Overlaps and differences in the core symptoms of patients with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and patients with borderline personality disorder
pmc-13358382.creator: Anna Christen, Marialuisa Cavelti, Rolf-Dieter Stieglitz, Beatrice Abt-Mörstedt, Hannes Bitto, Patricia E. Newark, Franz Moggi, Kerstin Gabriel Felleiter, Niklaus Stulz, Andreas Riedel, Salvatore Corbisiero
pmc-13358382.description: BackgroundIndividuals with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and individuals with borderline personality disorder (BPD) show symptomatic overlaps. They both suffer from deficits in emotional regulation, are impulsive and have problems with their self-concept. Therefore, a precise diagnostic differentiation is of great importance. The aim of this study was to find symptom overlaps and differences in patients with ADHD and BPD.

pmc-13415810.title: Geranylgeraniol as a Modulator of Mevalonate Pathway Disruption: A Scoping Review of Cellular Mechanisms and Skeletal Outcomes in Osteoporosis Models
pmc-13415810.creator: Sophia Ogechi Ekeuku, Mohammed Farhan Abed Al Salman, Nur Vaizura Mohamad, Sok Kuan Wong, Kok-Yong Chin
pmc-13415810.description: Background/Objectives: Geranylgeraniol (GGOH), an isoprenoid intermediate of the mevalonate pathway, regulates bone cell viability and function, particularly by mitigating cellular toxicity induced by nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates (N-BPs). Despite this, its role in osteoporosis remains underexplored. This scoping review synthesises evidence on the effects of GGOH in in vitro and in vivo models of osteoporosis.
